reviewed_result.shape_classification: For flattened NVDLA CMAC_CORE_mac, many independent states are consistently faster than CPU. Repeated steps are still faster when enough independent states amortize launch overhead, but single-state repeated-step shapes remain weak or slower.
reviewed_result.non_flat_status: Non-flattened timed Syms speedup remains unclaimed because CPU/GPU coverage-output semantics still mismatch after scheduler/time alignment attempts.

modern_nn_gap_review.finding: The current NVDLA CMAC evidence answers a scoped CNN-era MAC/datapath question, but it does not exercise the dominant current Transformer, LLM, VLM, or generative inference paths.
missing_capabilities: Transformer Q/K/V projection and attention score datapath
KV-cache resident state and prefill/decode serving split
model or graph ingestion and fused operator scheduling

selected_next_gap.reason: The current objective still needs a benchmark that is representative of modern NN inference; expanding older NVDLA CMAC shapes would add less information than defining a minimal attention-style RTL seed.
candidate_policy: Prefer an existing source-backed RTL target if available in third_party or overlays.
Keep one active seed target until the first attention-style CPU-vs-hybrid metric exists.
Require coverage-output equivalence before any speedup claim.
Measure at least one state-parallel shape and one repeated-step/token-like shape.
Preserve NVDLA CMAC results as scoped CNN-era evidence, not broad NN evidence.

must_record: candidate RTL source or explicit source gap

non_claims: not model accuracy or numerical inference correctness
not a broad CPU-vs-hybrid speedup claim
